data.one_liner: Utility‑first Tailwind‑style styling for Flutter using className strings.
data.what_it_does: Parses Tailwind‑like class strings into optimized Flutter widget trees. Provides W‑prefixed widgets and a theming system that supports dark mode, responsive breakpoints, and platform variants.
use_when: You already know Tailwind and want to reuse its syntax in Flutter
You need rapid UI building with built‑in dark‑mode and responsive support
You prefer a declarative styling layer over manual widget composition
avoid_when: You require fine‑grained custom animations or layout beyond Tailwind tokens
You need the smallest possible bundle size
You want strict type‑safe widget APIs without string‑based styling
strengths: Familiar Tailwind syntax reduces learning curve
Cuts boilerplate by turning class strings into widgets
Built‑in dark mode, responsive breakpoints, and platform variants
weaknesses: Adds an abstraction layer that can hide widget details
Unknown or misspelled tokens are silently ignored in release builds
Limited to the provided token set; extending requires package changes
data.setup_notes: Add the package, wrap the app with WindTheme, and start using W-prefixed widgets with className strings.

alternatives.name: material_ui
alternatives.why_pick_it: Standard Material widgets with full type safety and no string‑based styling
